### Headline summary
- 1Password disclosed a breach where an attacker accessed an employee's GitHub account to steal customer data and source code, though vaults remained secure. ([Cointelegraph.com News](https://cointelegraph.com/news/1password-hacker-stole-customer-names-and-emails-but-vaults-safe?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound), [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/1password-breach-exposes-customer-data-internal-source-code/))
- Drupal issued a warning for a critical access control vulnerability that is currently being actively exploited to take over websites. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/drupal-warns-of-new-highly-critical.html), [Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/drupal-website-takeover-flaw/))
- CISA added ten vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including flaws in Mitel, Juniper, and HPE products. ([Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/204014/hacking/u-s-cisa-adds-hpe-juniper-session-smart-conductor-and-session-smart-router-flaw-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html), [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-10-vulnerabilities.html))

### Drupal critical vulnerability exploited in the wild
Drupal warned of a highly critical access control flaw, CVE-2026-136716, that allows website takeover and is currently being actively exploited by attackers. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/drupal-warns-of-new-highly-critical.html), [Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/drupal-website-takeover-flaw/), [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/drupal-installer-patch-left-a-gap-attackers-are-already-exploiting/), [Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/204085/security/drupal-warns-of-new-critical-flaw-exploited-in-the-wild.html))

### 1Password breach via employee GitHub account
1Password disclosed a security incident where an attacker accessed an employee's corporate GitHub account to steal customer names, emails, and internal source code, though customer vaults remained secure. ([Cointelegraph.com News](https://cointelegraph.com/news/1password-hacker-stole-customer-names-and-emails-but-vaults-safe?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound), [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/1password-breach-exposes-customer-data-internal-source-code/), [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/26/1password-breach-github-customer-records/), [Infosecurity Magazine](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/1password-github-account-backend/))

### CISA adds Mitel, Juniper, and other flaws to KEV
The US CISA added 10 vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including flaws in Mitel MiCollab, Juniper, HPE, Danfoss, and Vates Xen products. ([Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/204014/hacking/u-s-cisa-adds-hpe-juniper-session-smart-conductor-and-session-smart-router-flaw-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html), [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-10-vulnerabilities.html), [Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/cisa-adds-10-flaws-to-kev/))

### New GeoServer RCE exploit chain seen in the wild two days after disclosure
Attackers have begun probing a chain of five GeoServer vulnerabilities that enables unauthenticated remote code execution, just two days after the open source geospatial server project disclosed the flaws. Security firm watchTowr, which operates a global network of honeypot servers, reported that i… ([CSO Online](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4253667/new-geoserver-rce-exploit-chain-seen-in-the-wild-two-days-after-disclosure.html))

### State-backed hackers use ARTEX AI framework
Microsoft confirmed that state-backed hackers and financially motivated groups are using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework to steal credentials and breach networks. ([Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/artex-ai-agents-2/), [Infosecurity Magazine](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/chinese-north-korea-artex/))

### North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
The threat actors behind the PolinRider campaign have been observed planting a Python loader in GitHub repositories, as evidence emerges that the activity may have started as far back as February 2025. "The loader hides in a small utils package or in conftest.py," SafeDep said in a report published… ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/north-korea-linked-polinrider-poisons.html))

### Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension
The Remus infostealer is stealing Gmail messages through a stealthy malicious Chrome extension, a capability the malware operators marketed as a zero-day exploit in Google's email service. ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/remus-malware-steals-gmail-messages-via-fake-google-sheets-extension/))

### FIFA confirms cyberattack on internal documents
FIFA confirmed that hackers gained unauthorized access to a limited set of personal and business information, with attackers claiming access to 12.2 GB of sensitive internal documents. ([Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/fifa-alleged-breach/), [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/fifa-says-it-has-been-victim-of-a-cyberattack-accessing-personal-and-business-information/))
